name: Lat pulldown
pattern: Vertical pull while seated: the hands pull a bar or handles from overhead down to the upper chest, shoulder blades moving down and back.
setup: Thighs locked under the pad, feet flat.
Grip the bar about 1.5 times shoulder width, palms away.
Sit tall with a slight lean back, chest up, arms straight.

steps.text: Arms straight overhead, let the shoulders rise a little to start long.
Pull your shoulder blades down first, arms still straight.
Drive your elbows down and back until the bar reaches your upper chest.
Let the bar rise under control until your arms are straight again.

cues.cue: Pull to the front, to your upper chest, never behind the neck.
cues.why: The front pulldown works the lats at least as well; behind-the-neck shifts work to the biceps and rear delt and stresses the shoulder.
Grips from 1 to 2 times shoulder width give similar lat activity; the wide grip lowered the load lifted.

cues.cue: Think 'elbows to your back pockets', not 'hands down'.
cues.why: Coached focus on the lats raised lat activity in beginners.

cues.cue: Shoulders down and away from your ears as you pull.
cues.why: Depressing and retracting the shoulder blades is how the lower and middle trapezius share the pull.

cues.cue: Small lean back, about 10-20°, then hold it still.
cues.why: Leaning back and rocking turns the pulldown into a row and uses momentum.

breathing: Breathe out as you pull down, in as the bar rises.

tempo.note: Pull in about 1 second, squeeze, return in 2.

mistakes.name: Behind the neck
mistakes.looks: The head drops forward and the bar comes down behind it.
mistakes.fix: Lean back slightly and bring the bar to your upper chest.
mistakes.why: It forces the shoulder into end-range external rotation with the arm raised, and offers no extra lat work.

mistakes.name: Rocking back
mistakes.looks: The trunk swings far back on every rep to drag the bar down.
mistakes.fix: Pick a lighter weight; keep a fixed small lean.
mistakes.why: Momentum and a large lean change the exercise into a row and reduce lat demand in the top range.

mistakes.name: Shoulders stay up
mistakes.looks: The arms bend but the shoulders stay hunched near the ears.
mistakes.fix: Start each rep by pulling your shoulders down.
mistakes.why: Upper-trapezius dominance replaces the lower and mid trapezius work the pull should train.

mistakes.name: Short range
mistakes.looks: The bar stops at the forehead, or the arms never straighten at the top.
mistakes.fix: Bar to the upper chest; straight arms at the top each rep.
mistakes.why: Full range lets the lats work from a long position to a short one.

safety: Shoulder pain: use a neutral grip and pull to the front only.
Hold the bar until it is back on the stack; do not let the weight snap your arms up.

variants.change: Close or neutral grip: similar lat work, a little more biceps; elbows travel close to the body.
Palms up: more biceps; the elbows finish in front of the trunk.
Hands about 2 times shoulder width: slightly less load, similar lat activity.
Behind-the-neck pulldown: not recommended; more biceps and rear delt, more shoulder stress.
One arm at a time: trunk resists side bending; the hand can turn in as it comes down.
Kneeling, standing or lying at a cable: same arm path, trunk stays tall and braced.

subtypes.name: Kneeling or standing pulldown
subtypes.change: Kneeling or standing facing a high cable or band, trunk slightly forward; same arm and shoulder-blade path.

subtypes.name: Floor pulldown
subtypes.change: Lying face up or down on the floor, arms overhead; pull the elbows down to the sides.

metrics.label: Elbow bend
metrics.good: 100-120 at the bottom, near 0 at the top

metrics.label: Bar to
metrics.good: upper chest, in front of the face

motion.basis: Grip width effects from andersen2014 and signorile2002; front vs behind-neck from sperandei2009; scapular pattern taken from the pull-up (prinold2016) and humeral-elevation data (escamilla2009), values estimated. Lean-back angle and seated hip and knee angles are coaching convention.
